added_failure_basis: The manifest declares no baseline_suite or after_suite key, so the two arms were read from the reviewed run's own archived gate logs: gate-base.log (revision 8d010aef2), which ran tests/test_a_crashed_producer_is_restarted.py, tests/test_follower_freshness.py and tests/test_resume_reaps_its_child.py's sibling three-file set with 1 failed + 6 errors, and gate-head-final.log (revision 1335254cc, three commits before the reviewed head and differing from it only by a docs fragment) with 3 failed + 6 errors. The 6 ERROR ids and test_repeated_crashes_reach_a_reported_limit appear in both; the set difference is the two ids recorded here. Neither is attributable: gate-base-suspects.log shows test_crashed_producer_reoccupies_the_seat[crash] failing on an unmodified extraction of the base revision (1 failed, 2 passed), and gate-base-resume.log and gate-head-resume-serial.log both record 6 passed EXIT=0 for test_resume_reaps_its_child.py, so that id is a parallel-load flake (gate-head-clean-suspects.log: 15 passed when the suspect set runs alone). The base arm was scoped to the files that failed at head, which is sound for attribution but means the '0 added' figure is not a full-tree base measurement.

evidence_inputs: Reproduction of the defect at base: the mutation log gate-head-importers.log carries the new test's first case red under eight-way parallelism, and negative-control.log applies 'inherited = []' at 0ad7fadfc and shows the inherited child left in state Z with EXIT=1, which is the zombie the plan describes.
The reaper start is the pre-existing _ensure_launched_worker_reaper call at dispatch_launch.py:523, reached through the new 'adoption' flag rather than by a second start path.

I verified the ruff delta at the reviewed head myself: six findings across the four changed files, byte-identical in id and location to the base arm's six (the W292 the ruff-delta.log recorded was removed by 1335254cc), and ruff format --check reports the same single file (dispatch_launch.py) reformatted at both revisions.
The importer gate ran at 1335254cc, three commits before the reviewed head; 0def2d8a7 adds only the evidence fragment, so no code differs between the gate tree and the reviewed head.

The reviewed head is not an ancestor of this review worktree's HEAD, so the landed change is not yet on main and the named test cannot be re-run in this tree; the gate result read here is the recorded one.

findings.text: non-blocking: _inherited_child_pids adopts every child the process already holds, not only the ones the previous image left, so a child the new image started before this call is registered and the reaper's waitpid consumes an exit status its owning Popen.wait() then cannot read. In watch_ticker and admit_until_stopped the call is the first statement, so the exposure there is narrow, but the follower reaches it at crew_follow_commands.py:2915 after building the ticker grid and taking its checkpoint.

non-blocking: test_a_child_the_new_image_starts_keeps_its_own_exit_status calls the adoption inside the pytest process and only starts its child afterwards, so it covers the after-ordering alone; the before-ordering case in the finding above is unguarded, and any child pytest already holds at line 147 is silently adopted into the shared registry for the rest of the module.

non-blocking: the artifacts line claims '0 added against base', but the manifest carries no baseline_suite or after_suite key and the archived base arm gate-base.log covers only 3 of the 124 gate files; the claim is true in substance (gate-base-suspects.log shows test_crashed_producer_reoccupies_the_seat[crash] red at base and the resume file green at both revisions when run alone) but the record overstates the measurement it rests on.
